constraints.project: Python standard library; synthetic local fixtures; fixed temporal split; train-only fit; deterministic local JSON; no cloud accounts, SDK calls, enrollment, exam registration, purchases, or deployed services.
constraints.studyBudget: Study is inside the 165-minute engineering total, never added outside it.
constraints.baselineName: Fixed global nonpersonalized popularity baseline from distinct positive training viewers per media; do not call it a trained ML model.
constraints.distinctViewerPolicy: Distinct positive training viewers per media and a fixed global cutoff list. The local protocol is not an implementation of Amazon Personalize service semantics.
constraints.predictionCount: At most three distinct media IDs; fewer candidates never change the precision denominator of 3.
constraints.recallTruth: All distinct positive holdout media IDs for each included evaluation user, including candidate-unreachable future items.

requiredPrimaryReferences.title: Popularity-Count recipe
requiredPrimaryReferences.focus: A nonpersonalized baseline ranks items by unique interacting users and returns the same list to everyone. Read this idea, not service setup. A local implementation is not an Amazon Personalize deployment.

requiredPrimaryReferences.title: Datasets: Dividing the original dataset
requiredPrimaryReferences.focus: Keep evaluation separate from fitting; repeated test-guided changes can contaminate assessment. This reading does not prescribe this project's temporal policy.

requiredPrimaryReferences.title: RankingMetrics: precisionAt and recallAt
requiredPrimaryReferences.focus: Precision@K divides relevant retrieved items by K even when fewer than K predictions are returned. Recall@K divides relevant retrieved items by the full ground-truth set size. Compute per-user results, then macro-average each metric separately.
requiredPrimaryReferences.caveat: Read metric definitions only; do not install Spark or import PySpark.

planningGuardrails: All reading, short videos if already accessible, implementation, tests, and evidence must fit the engineering budget; optional videos substitute for matching conceptual reading, not add an extra course workload.
Preserve the existing fixed split and eligibility contract unless an explicit plan change documents why. Do not silently import Amazon Personalize service split semantics.

Use train-only distinct user-item counts if following the primary popularity reference. If choosing event-count popularity instead, name that separate design explicitly and test repeated-user amplification.
Keep the same global ordering for all users to make the nonpersonalized claim honest. Adding user-specific seen-item filtering changes final results and requires a declared protocol.
Include hand-calculated metric cases, tied counts, zero-count items, all-miss rankings, duplicate recommendation rejection, invalid K, leakage sentinel, and byte-stable reruns.
Treat synthetic metrics as demonstrations that calculations work, not evidence of personalization, causal lift, real-user quality, fairness, or production readiness.

Freeze K=3, tie handling, positive-event relevance, candidate eligibility, and empty-truth policy before scoring. Precision denominator always remains 3. Recall retains all distinct positive holdout targets, including candidate-unreachable future items.
